validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE — CONFIRMED (high). The sheet's only citation is a single generic aggregate source (OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012, p.75) that does not by itself name this line, which is an existence red flag; but two INDEPENDENT origins confirm the physical pipeline. (1) Reuters wire (02 Jun 2025), carried in Arabic by Al-Ittihad (aletihad.ae) and in English by Pipeline & Gas Journal: 'a pipeline carrying gas from Iraq's northern Kirkuk oilfields to power stations [in Baiji]' operated by state-run North Gas Co. (NGC); a corrosion-crack blast ~55 km west of Kirkuk halted flow. (2) Shafaq News' OWN field reporting (not the wire — different facts: names Al-Maradia village in Hawija district, reports a security cordon and closure of the Kirkuk-Baiji road) confirms 'a gas pipeline between Baiji gas station and Kirkuk province.' Two independent field/wire origins agreeing = high. CLASSIFICATION — correct: this is a gas TRANSMISSION trunk delivering Kirkuk associated/field gas to Baiji power stations, not a gathering/plant-internal line and not one of the region's crude/products lines. Explicitly NOT a duplicate of the crude 'Kirkuk-Baiji-Baghdad Oil Pipeline' nor the OPC Baiji-Kirkuk oil-products line (both are oil, separate commodity), and NOT the recent 16-in Khor Mor->Kirkuk power-station gas line (Jambur/NGC branch, 1.05 km). DUPLICATE — none: no other gas-roster row is a Kirkuk->Baiji 24-in ~145 km line (P2233 North Gas-Taji is 438 km/16 in; P2232 North Gas-K1 is 34 km/18 in; P1842 Baiji-Al Mushraq runs Baiji->Mosul). ATTRIBUTION — confirmed: operator North Gas Co., a Ministry of Oil state company (Owner1 = Iraq Ministry of Oil OK); FuelSource = Kirkuk (Kirkuk oilfield gas, per Reuters) OK; endpoints Kirkuk (start) -> Baiji, Saladin (end) OK. SPEC — CAVEAT, low: LengthKnown 145 km, Diameter 24 in, Capacity 0.89 bcm/y, ConstructionYear 2012, SegmentCost USD 127,000,000 all trace to OPEC ASB only; I could not independently corroborate any of them (OPEC ASB PDF returned HTTP 402; searches surfaced mostly 16-in gas lines in this corridor, so the 24-in figure is uncorroborated). No source was found that CONTRADICTS the values, so this is an unverified caveat, not a confirmed conflict. Kirkuk-Baiji straight-line is ~100 km, so 145 km implies a ~45% routing detour (consistent with the Hawija-district blast site on the corridor).

fills.researcher_notes: Both sources describe an in-service gas pipeline (flow halted by a June 2025 blast, then repaired) between Kirkuk and Baiji -> operating confirmed.
Both explicitly call it a natural-gas pipeline (خط أنابيب للغاز / gas pipeline).
Reuters wire: gas sourced from Kirkuk's northern oilfields; Shafaq: gas from Kirkuk province. FuelSource = Kirkuk confirmed.

Both name a Kirkuk->Baiji gas pipeline. Baiji is in Saladin (Salah al-Din) governorate; end endpoint and province confirmed. Start given at province granularity (Kirkuk); a precise start facility is not named in these sources.

Operated by state-run North Gas Co. (NGC), a Ministry of Oil company (Reuters/Al-Ittihad); Shafaq attributes it to state North Oil Company. Both point to Iraqi state (Ministry of Oil) ownership; supports Owner1 = Iraq Ministry of Oil 100%. Note operator is specifically NGC — consider recording North Gas Company as operator.
145 km rests only on OPEC ASB (the sheet's own source). No independent source found. Not contradicted; unverified. Kirkuk-Baiji straight-line ~100 km, so 145 km implies a routing detour.

24 in rests only on OPEC ASB. No independent source found; regionally most documented NGC/OPC gas-to-power lines are 16 in, so the 24-in figure warrants a check but is not contradicted by any specific source for THIS line.
0.89 bcm/y (~86 MMcf/d) rests only on OPEC ASB. No independent corroboration; left as-is, unverified.

ConstructionYear 2012 rests only on OPEC ASB and may be an ASB reporting-year artifact rather than a build date; the corridor's Kirkuk gas infrastructure is far older (Shafaq cites pipeline age as a corrosion factor). Unverified.
USD 127,000,000 has no independent corroboration and no SegmentCostYear recorded; unverified. Recommend leaving flagged rather than green.

waypoints.name: Hawija district vicinity (blast site ~55 km W of Kirkuk, near Al-Maradia village)

routes.corridor_desc: Runs west-southwest from the Kirkuk oilfield gas system (North Gas Company, Kirkuk governorate) toward the Baiji power stations in Saladin governorate, ~145 km per OPEC ASB (straight-line ~100 km, so a modest detour). Independent field reporting places the corridor through/near Hawija district, Kirkuk governorate: the June 2025 corrosion blast was ~55 km west of Kirkuk (Reuters) at Al-Maradia village in Hawija (Shafaq), which sits on the Kirkuk->Baiji axis (the Kirkuk-Baiji road was closed at the blast site). Bound is MEDIUM: three named anchor points (Kirkuk start, Hawija-district midpoint, Baiji end) but no published route geometry; the precise start facility and exact alignment are not sourced.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from two independent origins (Reuters wire; Shafaq field report) naming a Kirkuk-oilfield-to-Baiji-power-stations gas line. Coordinates are the well-known centroids of Kirkuk city (35.4681, 44.3922), Baiji town (34.9294, 43.4887) and Hawija town (35.3167, 43.7667) used as defensible anchors for named places; NO coordinate was invented. Al-Maradia village exact coordinates could not be sourced, so the waypoint is given at Hawija-district granularity and described in words. The precise start (which Kirkuk field/gas plant) is not named by the sources.

summary: P2231 confirmed real & correctly classified (gas transmission, Kirkuk oilfields -> Baiji power stations, North Gas Co./Ministry of Oil) via 2 independent origins; specs (145 km/24 in/0.89 bcm/y/2012/$127M) rest on OPEC ASB only and are unverified caveats.
